name: Vespid Dynamics Venomfly Micro-Drone Swarm VMS-3 'Murder Cloud'
description: An advanced evolution of Vespid's micro-drone platform, the VMS-3 deploys a cloud of 50 insect-sized drones that collectively form a mobile toxic fog. Each drone carries a micro-reservoir of contact neurotoxin that it disperses through ultrasonic atomization while flying in a coordinated swarm pattern. The cloud of drones and toxin droplets moves as a coherent mass toward designated coordinates, flowing around obstacles and through openings as small as a ventilation grate. The swarm's collective intelligence allows it to pursue moving targets, avoid countermeasures, and saturate enclosed spaces. Individual drones have only 4 minutes of flight time, but the swarm staggers activation to maintain the cloud for up to 10 minutes.
specifications:
drone count: 50 per deployment canister
individual drone size: 1.5 cm wingspan
swarm cloud diameter: 3-8 meters
flight time: 4 minutes per drone, 10 minutes staggered swarm
toxin: Contact neurotoxin, incapacitation in 15 seconds of skin exposure
operating range: 300 meters from launch
navigation: Collective AI with coordinate targeting
weight: 2.5 kg per deployment canister
story_hooks: A Murder Cloud was deployed in a sealed corporate boardroom during a shareholder meeting — the attack was precise, premeditated, and someone had detailed knowledge of the building's ventilation layout.
A VMS-3 swarm was intercepted mid-flight and its navigation data extracted — the coordinates lead to a target who has no idea they were marked for assassination.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact cylindrical canister resembling a high-tech aerosol dispenser, sleek and sinister. The housing suggests contained chaos — a sealed vessel of distributed death. At first glance, it could pass for a cologne atomizer or industrial lubricant can, but the precision engineering and warning markings betray its true purpose.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 12 cm, Diameter: 4.5 cm, Launch port diameter: 0.8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light — only 2.5 kg total, creating a jarring contrast between its lethal payload and its handheld convenience. Sits in the palm without resistance, belying the 50-unit swarm it contains.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite polymer shell with internal titanium-reinforced micro-reservoir grid. Launch mechanism uses surgical-grade stainless steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal black with a subtle iridescent oil-slick sheen across the upper hemisphere, suggesting the volatile chemical payload beneath. The finish is deliberately unmarked to suggest illegality.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with acid-green accent lines tracing the micro-drone egress ports in a hexagonal grid pattern. Tiny bioluminescent warning symbols glow faintly in the dark: Φ-marked prohibition stamps.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare titanium knurling on the lower half, deliberately uncomfortable to discourage casual handling. The upper release mechanism is smooth, tempered polymer — cold and surgical.
distinctive_features: Six micro-apertures arranged in a hexagonal pattern around the upper circumference, each barely visible but precisely machined
A small digital readout (3mm LED screen) displaying drone count and battery status in sickly amber numerals
Faint metallic striations visible through semi-translucent polymer sections, hinting at the drone storage grid within
A thumb-press activation point with a recessed safety cap featuring a biometric lock
Microscopic etching around the base: 'VESPID DYNAMICS | VMS-3 | DEPLOYMENT ONLY | DO NOT OPEN'
A small pressurized indicator gauge on the side — a thin red line that moves with internal drone readiness
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS logo embossed in raised letters on the lower front, deeply stamped to prevent erosion. Serial number laser-etched vertically along the rear seam. Tier 5 warning symbols (red Φ symbol and crossed-out city icon) stamped on opposite sides.
physical_description.condition_typical: Street units show scuffing and micro-abrasions from illicit courier handling. Black finish develops a faded, weathered patina from repeated exposure to humid Great Lakes air. Some units show evidence of hasty field repairs or component swaps. Biometric locks may be scratched or bypassed. The readout screens frequently flicker or display corrupted data on older units.
